_comment: Codex Micro -> whichever app has focus. Keys map to VERBS; each target says how a verb is performed in that app. Physical layout confirmed 2026-08-28: AG00-AG05 top row L-R, ACT06-ACT12 bottom row L-R, ACT11 ignored (the wide mic cap fires ACT10+ACT11 together).
_dictation_strategy: Use the app's OWN dictation where it has one, fall back to the local Parakeet pipeline where it does not. That is why `dictate` is a per-target verb rather than a single global behaviour: 'parakeet' runs the local pipeline (hold to record, release to transcribe and insert), {"hold": "<chord>"} holds a chord down for as long as the mic key is held (for apps whose own hotkey is push-to-talk), and {"start": "<chord>", "stop": "<chord>"} sends one chord on press and another on release (for apps with separate start/stop commands).
_passthrough_why: Codex desktop reads the SAME hidraw node as this bridge — hidraw allows multiple concurrent readers — and acts on the same keys with its own native Micro integration. Without this the mic key fires twice: Codex's dictation and ours. While a passthrough app has focus the bridge ignores every key and lets the app own the device. Extra spellings exist because Electron's Wayland app_id is the productName (`ChatGPT`) unless --class actually stuck (`codex-desktop`).

cursor._why: The Agents window does not act on keybindings.json. First measured 2026-08-28 (ctrl+shift+n, a default chord, works there; F13 and a custom ctrl+alt+d do not, while all three work in the main Cursor window). The rule was removed on 2026-09-16 on the strength of a recollection that F13 dictation had worked in Agents on atlas, and restored on 2026-09-17 when it did not: the log showed `ACT10 -> dictate start [F13] in Cursor` with no error, a 928 ms hold, and nothing recorded, against Cursor 3.20.21 with the Agents window the only Cursor window open. That is the exact symptom the removal note said to watch for. wtype and wlrctl both succeed, so the dispatch side is not at fault; the chord reaches the window and the window ignores it.

_grounded.send: Carter: the send key 'sends the transcripted line, its basically like enter'
_grounded.paste: grok-bot registers CmdOrCtrl+V as an Electron accelerator; Cursor is VS Code derived; ghostty uses ctrl+shift+v in a terminal
_grounded.grokbot.dictate: Grokbot's composer mic button is ctrl+d, and its KEYDOWN handler is a toggle: if already recording it stops, otherwise it starts. Its keyup handler only stops when the key was held past a threshold, AND it clears its own down-timestamp first, so a synthetic hold does not work: wtype cannot hold a key across two invocations (the virtual keyboard is destroyed when the process exits), so the app saw an instant press-release, latched, and then ignored the later release. Sending a COMPLETE ctrl+d on each edge is what gives hold-to-talk: the first keydown starts, the second stops.
_grounded.grokbot.dictate.preconditions: Two facts the ctrl+d handler enforces that the grokbot.dictate entry above does not record, both read from the bundle: it returns early unless isPromptFocused(), so raising the window is NOT enough and the composer itself must have focus; and the hold threshold is exactly 500 ms (QPn), which is how long the key must be held for the keyup edge to stop recording.
_grounded.terminal.approve: CLI agent permission prompts select on the number key, and terminal.deny on Escape — the same thing bin/mh already does for herdr
_grounded.cursor.dictate: Cursor's composer mic button is composer.toggleVoiceDictation (composer.cancelVoiceDictation also exists), read out of the workbench bundle. It ships with no default keybinding, so ~/.config/Cursor/User/keybindings.json maps F13 to it and the bridge sends F13 on both edges. It is a toggle, so down-then-up gives hold-to-talk.
_grounded.t3code.dictate: T3 Code has NO built-in dictation: its only Dictation reference is a comment about Wispr Flow, an external tool, pasting into it. So it gets the local pipeline like the terminal does.
_grounded.cursor.dictate.agents-window: Restored 2026-09-17 after a one-day removal; see windowVariants._why for the full timeline and the measurement that settled it. Keep this rule: the main Cursor window uses its own dictation (F13 -> composer.toggleVoiceDictation), the Agents window cannot, and falls back to the local pipeline. If a future Cursor build fixes Agents, the tell is F13 working there by hand, not a recollection.
_grounded.cursor.effort: composer.cycleModelParameter (reasoning effort) and composer.cycleModel, read out of the workbench bundle alongside composer.openModelToggle. Neither ships a default keybinding, so Cursor's keybindings.json maps F14 and F15 to them. LIMITATION: these are one-way cycle commands, so the knob advances the effort level in the same direction whichever way you turn it. It wraps, so you can still reach every level.
_grounded.grokbot.new-session: sand.newAgent, hotkey mod+n, read out of the renderer bundle in Grokbot 0.24.0's app.asar. Its action object carries isEnabledInContentEditable:!0, so it fires even while the composer has focus. `mod` resolves per platform in the hotkey layer (`const t = e ? "meta" : "ctrl"`, keyed off isMacPlatform), which is ctrl on Linux.
_grounded.grokbot.deny: Escape, and it is the app's own advertised binding: the pending-permission component's button reads "Deny once (Esc)". It installs a window keydown listener in CAPTURE phase that calls the deny resolution. Bare Escape only: the handler bails on any modifier, on event.repeat, on defaultPrevented, and when the event target is an input, textarea or select. The composer is a contenteditable div and none of those three, so a synthetic Escape still denies while the prompt has focus.
_grounded.grokbot.approve: Stays null because Grokbot 0.24.0 has NO keyboard path to approve. Searched the whole renderer bundle: "Allow once", "Allow automatically" and "Approve" exist only as button labels, no accelerator is registered for any of them, and no approve handler sits near a key check. Deny is keyboard-reachable and approve is not, which is the safe asymmetry, so this is a missing feature upstream rather than something to guess a chord for.
_grounded.grokbot.diff: Stays null because there is no diff command in the app at all. The renderer's command registry holds 16 sand.* actions and none of them is a diff view.
_grounded.grokbot.effort: Deliberately unmapped: Grokbot exposes a single model with no effort control, so there is nothing for the knob to select. The renderer does expose sand.nextAgent (alt+down) and sand.previousAgent (alt+up), which would give the knob something to do, but the keys map assigns ENC_CW/ENC_CC globally to effort-up/effort-down, so repurposing them here would also take Cursor's only reasoning-effort control away. Left alone on purpose.

_needs_input: t3code effort/model: T3 Code has modelPicker.toggle, modelPicker.jump.1-9, reasoningEffort and effortLevel as bindable command names, but its config dir holds only Electron profile data, so there is no keybindings file to write and no discoverable defaults. Assign chords in its own settings UI, then set them here.

terminal effort/model: CLI agents switch models with a slash command rather than a keystroke (Claude Code uses /model), so a knob detent has no natural mapping. Could send literal text if that is wanted.
new-session / approve / deny / diff for cursor and t3code. Grokbot is settled: new-session and deny are mapped from its own bundle, approve and diff are unreachable there (see _grounded)
